paige.l: hey team :wave: first day here — trying to build the inference runtime from source on my dev box (Ubuntu 22.04, RTX 3090). followed README: cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build -j16. hitting linker and libstdc++ symbol errors, not sure which direction to try next. log snippet below:

paige.l: ```
[ 87%] Linking CXX executable bin/rw_infer
/usr/bin/ld: build/lib/libcuda_kernels.a(kernel.o): in function `init_cuda()':
kernel.cpp:(.text+0x1f0): undefined reference to `__cudaRegisterFatBinary'
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.29' not found (required by build/lib/libthirdparty.so)
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
make[2]: *** [src/CMakeFiles/rw_infer.dir/build.make:122: bin/rw_infer] Error 1
make[1]: *** [CMakeFiles/Makefile2:140: src/CMakeFiles/rw_infer.dir/all] Error 2
```

paige.l: nvcc --version shows CUDA 12.1, driver is 535.54.03 according to nvidia-smi, conda env python 3.11, system gcc default is 11 but I have 9 installed too. any quick checks on what usually causes this?

devon: welcome, paige! :wave: a few quick things we've seen: first check driver vs toolkit (you did, looks okay). the GLIBCXX error usually means libstdc++ on your PATH is older than what some prebuilt thirdparty was compiled against. run `strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 | grep GLIBCXX` to see what versions are present.

devon: also nvcc links against the host gcc toolchain — try switching to gcc-9/g++-9 for the build: `sudo update-alternatives --set gcc /usr/bin/gcc-9 && sudo update-alternatives --set g++ /usr/bin/g++-9` then clear build dir and rebuild. we generally recommend gcc 9 or 11 for CUDA12 on Ubuntu22.

samir: if you want the fastest repro isolation, use our dev container: `docker run --rm -it redwood/dev-build:cuda12.1-ubuntu22.04 /bin/bash` — it has the right gcc, cuda, and cuDNN versions that CI uses. avoids host libstdc++ mismatch.

nina: quick note on the __cudaRegisterFatBinary symbol: that often appears when object files compiled with different nvcc/host compiler flags are linked together. Make sure all submodules are cleaned (`git submodule foreach --recursive git clean -fdx`) and that you run cmake from a fresh build directory. also set `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75` for 3090 to avoid PTX/arch mixups.

paige.l: thanks — switched to gcc-9 and cleared build dir, now link gets past the GLIBCXX failure but I hit a cudnn symbol missing: `undefined reference to cudnnGetVersion`. I don't have system cuDNN installed (I thought CUDA toolkit shipped it).

devon: CUDA toolkit no longer bundles full cuDNN usually. for local dev either install system cuDNN (apt or from nvidia) or use the docker image (it already contains cuDNN). we don't check cuDNN into repo due to licensing. CI uses a cached cuDNN package.

samir: if you want a quick local hack, set `-DUSE_SYSTEM_CUDNN=OFF` to build a CPU-only fallback for now, but some features will be disabled. better: use the dev container.

build-bot: [CI] build/runtime-linux-cuda - latest commit 0a1b2c3 - failure on self-hosted runner (missing cuDNN)

nina: i updated the onboarding checklist this morning with a small section on dev toolchain and docker usage — pinned to the channel. paige, if you hit more specific errors paste the full `nvidia-smi` and `gcc --version` output and we can pair.

paige.l: awesome, i'll try the docker image and report back. also could someone add a short note to the README about recommended system gcc versions? I tripped over that.

devon: yep will add a short note and link our docker image. if you're free later we can do a quick screenshare and finish your setup. :thumbsup:

paige.l: thanks all — appreciate the quick help! :raised_hands:
